item.title: Predicting Laptop Resale Value From Age
item.stimulus: An electronics reseller fit a least-squares regression line to the resale values of 15 laptops of the same model. The laptops were between 1 and 4 years old. The regression equation, found using technology, is ŷ = 640 − 85x, where x is the age of the laptop in years and ŷ is the predicted resale value in dollars.

parts.prompt: Use the model to predict the resale value of a laptop that is 3 years old. Is this prediction an interpolation or an extrapolation? Explain.

criteria.text: Substitutes x = 3 into ŷ = 640 − 85x and gets a predicted value of 385 dollars.
criteria.evidence: Response replaces x with 3 in the regression equation and reports 385 dollars.
criteria.fix: Replace x with the given value in the regression equation, calculate carefully, and report the predicted response with its units.

criteria.text: Classifies the prediction at 3 years as interpolation because 3 is within the interval of age values (1 to 4 years) used to fit the line.
criteria.evidence: Response says interpolation and compares 3 with the fitted interval of 1 to 4 years.
criteria.fix: Compare the x-value with the smallest and largest x-values in the data: inside is interpolation, outside is extrapolation.

parts.prompt: Use the model to predict the resale value of a laptop that is 7 years old. Is this prediction an interpolation or an extrapolation? Explain.

criteria.text: Substitutes x = 7 into ŷ = 640 − 85x and gets a predicted value of 45 dollars.
criteria.evidence: Response replaces x with 7 in the regression equation and reports 45 dollars.
criteria.fix: Replace x with the given value in the regression equation, calculate carefully, and report the predicted response with its units.

criteria.text: Classifies the prediction at 7 years as extrapolation because 7 is beyond the interval of age values (1 to 4 years) used to fit the line.
criteria.evidence: Response says extrapolation and compares 7 with the fitted interval of 1 to 4 years.
criteria.fix: Compare the x-value with the smallest and largest x-values in the data: inside is interpolation, outside is extrapolation.

parts.prompt: Which of your two predictions is more reliable? Explain.

criteria.text: States that the prediction at 3 years is more reliable than the prediction at 7 years, because 7 is extrapolation and predictions get less reliable the further age is beyond the data.
criteria.evidence: Response chooses the interpolated prediction as more reliable and gives extrapolation beyond the observed values as the reason.
criteria.fix: Say which prediction is inside the data range, and explain that extrapolated predictions become less reliable the farther they go beyond it.

item.model_answer:
(a) ŷ = 640 − 85x with x = 3 gives ŷ = 385 dollars. This is interpolation, because 3 years is within the interval of age values, 1 to 4 years, used to fit the line.

(b) With x = 7, ŷ = 45 dollars. This is extrapolation, because 7 years is beyond the interval of age values, 1 to 4 years, used to fit the line.

(c) The prediction at 3 years is more reliable. The prediction at 7 years is extrapolation, and predictions become less reliable the further age is beyond the data.
item.verification_python:
a = 640
b = -85
lo, hi = 1, 4
xn, xf = 3, 7
yn = a + b * xn
yf = a + b * xf
assert abs(yn - 385) < 1e-9
assert abs(yf - 45) < 1e-9
assert lo <= xn <= hi
assert xf > hi
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
